content: 1. Clarithromycin and Dronabinol: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of dronabinol by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal metabolism mediated by the CYP3A4 enzyme. Dronabinol is a substrate of CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 2. Clarithromycin and Dronedarone: Clarithromycin significantly increases the plasma levels and effects of dronedarone by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Both clarithromycin and dronedarone prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Co-administration is contraindicated; consider alternative therapies. 3. Clarithromycin and Droperidol: Both clarithromycin and droperidol prolong the QTc interval, which may lead to life-threatening arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor the patient closely with ECG. 4. Clarithromycin and Drospirenone: Drospirenone increases the plasma levels and effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely for any adverse effects. 5. Clarithromycin and Dutasteride: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of dutasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 6. Clarithromycin and Duvelisib: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of duvelisib by inhibiting both the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib exposure, raising the risk of toxicities. Modify therapy or monitor closely for adverse effects. 7. Clarithromycin and Edoxaban: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Dose adjustment may be required when co-administered with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the edoxaban dose to 30 mg once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for NVAF. Monitor closely. 8. Clarithromycin and Efavirenz: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Co-administration is contraindicated; consider alternative therapies. Efavirenz may also decrease clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 9. Clarithromycin and Elacestrant: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated; use an alternative drug. 10. Clarithromycin and Elagolix: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Modify therapy or monitor closely for adverse effects. 11. Clarithromycin and Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated; use an alternative drug. 12. Clarithromycin and Eletriptan: Clarithromycin significantly increases the plasma levels and effects of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated; use an alternative drug. 13. Clarithromycin and Eliglustat: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of eliglustat by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated in poor or intermediate metabolizers of eliglustat. For extensive metabolizers, reduce the eliglustat dose from 84 mg BID to 84 mg once daily. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors and strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors is contraindicated. 14. Clarithromycin and Eluxadoline: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of eluxadoline by inhibiting metabolism. Reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg BID if co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Clarithromycin and Elvitegravir: Clarithromycin increases the plasma levels and effects of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase its levels. Use caution and monitor closely.
